ext_description.message: Search for text on a webpage and replace it with different text.

saveApplyPageReload.message: Save and apply on page reload

Saveandapply.message: Save and apply on page reload

help_title.message: Help page for search and replace

next_vs_all_p1.message: To replace the first occurrence of the search term, press Replace Next. You can continue to press the button until there are no more occurrences.

next_vs_all_p2.message: To replace all occurrences of the search term, press Replace All.

next_vs_all_p3.message: There is currently no undo function. If you make a mistake, you can reload the page to restore the original text. However, you will lose any unsaved changes in text editors and in text input fields.

replace_editors.message: Replacing text in editors and text fields
replace_editors.description: Explanation about replacing text in editors and text fields

replace_editors_p1.message: To replace text in text editors or input boxes you should check the Input fields only? check box.
replace_editors_p1.description: Explanation about replacing text in editors and text fields

replace_editors_p3.message: This covers plain input and textarea boxes as well as rich text editors such as TinyMCE and CKEditor. Because nothing outside those fields is touched, it is the safest option on a complicated page, and the one to try first if a replacement appeared to break something.
replace_editors_p3.description: Explanation about replacing text in editors and text fields

Replacing_anywhere.message: Replacing text anywhere on the page
Replacing_anywhere.description: Explanation about replacing text anywhere on the page

Replacing_anywhere_p1.message: To replace text anywhere on the page, including within the HTML structure itself, check the Replace HTML? option. This allows you to replace text in all elements on the page, including regular text, text editors, input fields, and even HTML tags and attributes.
Replacing_anywhere_p1.description: Explanation about replacing text anywhere on the page

Replacing_anywhere_caption.message: Rewriting every example.com on the page, link addresses included.
Replacing_anywhere_caption.description: Caption for the Replace HTML screenshot

Replacing_anywhere_warning.message: This setup alters the page HTML and may break the page. You can restore the page by reloading, but you will lose any unsaved changes in text editors and in text input fields.
Replacing_anywhere_warning.description: Explanation about replacing text anywhere on the page

Matching_case.description: Explanation about matching the case of text

Matching_case_p1.message: If you need to replace THIS but not This then you should use the match case option.
Matching_case_p1.description: Explanation about matching the case of text

Matching_case_p2.message: The following setup will match Condo but not condo. It will replace Condo with apartment in text fields that are visible on the page.
Matching_case_p2.description: Explanation about matching the case of text

Matching_whole_p1.message: If you need to replace the word partial but not partially then you should use the Match whole word? option.

wildcards_and_regex.description: Explanation about wild cards and regular expressions

wildcards_and_regex_p1.message: If you need to match a partial search term then you should check the Regular Expressions check box and specify a wild card. You will need to have a very basic knowledge of regular expressions to use this feature. I recommend regexpal for testing
wildcards_and_regex_p1.description: Explanation about wild cards and regular expressions

wildcards_and_regex_p2.message: In the example below, 1\d1 means “a 1, then any digit, then a 1”, which matches 101, 111, 121 and so on up to 191.
wildcards_and_regex_p2.description: Worked example for the regular expression section

Replacing_wordpress_p1.message: The WordPress block editor keeps your post inside a frame of its own, separate from the rest of the admin page. The extension looks inside that frame for you, so no special options are needed: type your terms and press Replace All.

Replacing_wordpress_p2.message: If you are using the classic editor, or a page builder whose fields are ordinary text boxes, check Input fields only? first.

Replacing_wordpress_save.message: The replacement changes what is in the editor, not what is stored. Press Update in WordPress afterwards to keep it.
Replacing_wordpress_save.description: Reminder to save the post after replacing

Replacing_wordpress_caption.message: Editing a post in the block editor. No options are needed.

Save_apply.message: Save and apply on page reload
Save_apply.description: Save and apply on page reload

Save_apply_p1.message: You can check the Save and apply on page reload? check box to save your search and apply it on subsequent page reloads. These will take effect even after you have closed and re-opened your browser.
Save_apply_p1.description: Save and apply on page reload

Save_apply_editing.description: Save and apply on page reload

Save_apply_rules_caption.message: Each saved rule can be edited or deleted here.
Save_apply_rules_caption.description: Caption for the Saved Rules screenshot

Save_apply_multi_p1.message: If multiple rules apply to the same page, the rules will be applied in order of most specific to least specific. For example:

Save_apply_multi_p2.message: This means that any changes applied by the first rule will be fed into the subsequent rules. In the above example, the text Example will have been replaced by the rule matching http://www.example.com/a/deeper/nested/page. Subsequent rules will therefore have no effect.

Save_apply_multi_p3.message: You can edit the saved rules on the Saved Rules page, which the save icon in the popup opens. The URL Pattern field is a regular expression, which allows you to apply the same rule to many different websites.

ReportingIssuesWarning.message: Remember to reload any page that was already open when the extension was installed or updated. Until it is reloaded, the extension cannot reach it.

ReportingIssuesInfo.message: If the page has broken after using the extension, try refreshing the page, and then checking Input fields only? before performing a search and replace.

ReportingIssues_p1.message: If you find a bug, please provide a detailed report on the Chrome Extension Store or on GitHub.

Rate_on_store.message: Please rate ★★★★★ on Chrome Store if the extension helps you!

Troubleshooting_reload.message: Reload the page. A page that was already open when the extension was installed or updated cannot be reached until it is reloaded.

Troubleshooting_restricted.message: Browser pages such as chrome://, the Chrome Web Store and the extensions page are off limits to every extension, so nothing can be replaced there.

Troubleshooting_nomatch.message: If the count stays at zero, try Hidden content?, turn off Match case?, or check that the text is not an image.

no_saved_instances.description: message to tell user that no rules were found

matches.description: message to tell user how many instances of the search term were found

hidden_content_nav.description: Navigation link for hidden content help section

hidden_content_title.description: Title for hidden content help section

hidden_content_p1.message: By default, the extension only searches and replaces text that is visible on the page. If you need to search and replace text in hidden elements (such as collapsed sections, hidden divs, or elements with display: none), check the Hidden content? option.
hidden_content_p1.description: First paragraph explaining hidden content checkbox

hidden_content_p2.message: This is particularly useful when working with dynamic content that may be hidden initially but becomes visible through user interaction, or when you need to modify hidden form fields.
hidden_content_p2.description: Second paragraph explaining hidden content use cases

hidden_content_note.message: When Hidden content? is checked, the extension searches every element regardless of its visibility, which may result in a higher match count.

pageUnreachable.message: Search and Replace cannot reach this page. Reload the page and try again.

help_lede.message: How to find text on a page and change it — in ordinary text, in form fields, in editors, and automatically on every visit.

basics_p1.message: Open the popup from the toolbar, or with Ctrl+Shift+S. Type the text you are looking for into Search for and the text you want instead into Replace with, then press one of the two buttons at the bottom.
basics_p1.description: Help section on the popup layout

basics_p2.message: The number under the Search for box counts the matches left on the page, and updates as you type and as you replace. The row of icons along the top opens this help page, your recent searches, the About panel, the language setting, and your saved rules.
basics_p2.description: Help section on the popup layout

basics_caption.message: Four occurrences of Condo are left on the page.
basics_caption.description: Caption for the popup overview screenshot

options_p1.message: Every checkbox in the popup narrows or widens what is searched. They can be combined.

option_matchCase_desc.message: Only matches text with exactly the same capitalisation. Leave it unchecked and Condo, condo and CONDO all match.

option_inputFieldsOnly_desc.message: Limits the search to text boxes, text areas and rich text editors, and leaves the rest of the page alone. Use it whenever you are editing a form, a message or a post.

option_hiddenContent_desc.message: Includes elements you cannot currently see: collapsed panels, inactive tabs, off-screen menus and hidden form fields.

option_wholeWord_desc.message: Requires the match to be a whole word, so partial no longer matches inside partially.

option_isRegex_desc.message: Treats the search term as a regular expression instead of literal text.

option_replaceHTML_desc.message: Searches the page's HTML source rather than the text you can read, so tags, attributes, link addresses and alt text are all in scope.

option_save_desc.message: Stores the search as a rule and applies it again every time you open a matching page, even after you restart the browser.

hidden_content_caption.message: The same search finds six matches instead of four once hidden elements are included.
hidden_content_caption.description: Caption for the hidden content screenshot

history_p1.message: The clock icon in the popup lists your recent searches. Click one to put it back into the two boxes, or press Clear to empty the list.

history_p2.message: Swap, between the two boxes, exchanges the search and replace terms — handy for undoing a replacement you have just made, as long as the original text has not been typed anywhere else on the page.
history_p2.description: Help section on the swap button

history_p3.message: The cog icon holds the language setting. The extension is translated into Arabic, Chinese, English, German, Hindi, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, Russian and Spanish; anything not yet translated falls back to English.
history_p3.description: Help section on the language setting

saved_rules_lede.message: These searches run automatically every time you open a page whose address matches their URL pattern. The pattern is a regular expression, so one rule can cover a whole site.
saved_rules_lede.description: Introduction on the Saved Rules page

no_saved_instances_hint.message: Check "Save and apply on page reload?" in the popup to create one.
no_saved_instances_hint.description: Empty state on the Saved Rules page

no_history.message: Your recent searches will appear here.
no_history.description: Empty state of the History panel

history_removed.description: Shown in the History panel when the replacement term is empty

open_in_hint.message: The side panel stays open while you work on the page.

sidebar_p1.message: By default the extension opens as a popup under the toolbar button. A popup closes as soon as anything else takes the focus, so clicking into the page to check a replacement dismisses it and the terms have to be typed again.
sidebar_p1.description: Help section on the side panel

sidebar_p2.message: Choose Side panel under the cog icon to open in Chrome's side panel instead. It stays open while you work on the page, follows you from tab to tab, and can be dragged wider. Everything else works exactly as it does in the popup.
sidebar_p2.description: Help section on the side panel

sidebar_p3.message: The setting follows your Chrome profile, and the keyboard shortcut Ctrl+Shift+S opens whichever one you have chosen. The side panel needs Chrome 114 or newer; on anything older the setting is not shown.
sidebar_p3.description: Help section on the side panel

open_side_panel.description: Tooltip on the side panel icon in the popup

close_side_panel.description: Tooltip on the side panel icon when shown in the panel
